claims.sentence: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title> <jats:p>Multiple studies and analyses have demonstrated that use of an oronasal interface for delivery of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy can lead not only to higher pressure requirements, but also a higher residual apnea hypopnea Index (AHI) in patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).</jats:p> <jats:p>Report of Cases: We record a 75-year-old man with severe OSA, AHI of 38, and treated with CPAP 16 cm water.
